we have developed a deep neural network method for automatic detection and quantification of coronary artery and thoracic aorta calcifications in low dose chest CT scans, which is the first method that enables automatic cardiovascular risk assessment for the entire population undergoing lung cancer screening.

deep convolutional neural networks enable accurate automatic identification of coronary artery and thoracic aorta calcifications in all low-dosage chest CT scans acquired from subjects undergoing lung cancer screening, and that the presented approach enables reliable automatic cardiovascular disease risk assessment in these subjects.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of deep neural networks for the automated detection of coronary artery calcification in low-dose CT.

the development of a method for automatic quantification of coronary artery calcium (CAC) and other cardiovascular calcifications from low-dose CT scans acquired for the purpose of lung cancer screening.
the development of a deep learning-based method for detection of coronary artery calcifications in low dose CT scans of the chest.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented method provides a reliable automatic method for quantification of cardiovascular risk in low-dose CT scans.
the presented method is able to identify and quantify coronary calcifications in low dose chest CT scans.

the presented method is a reliable tool for automatic cardiovascular risk assessment and can be used to identify patients at increased cardiovascular risk in low-dose CT scans acquired in lung cancer screening.

we have shown that deep learning methods can be used to automatically detect coronary artery calcification in chest CTs with high sensitivity and specificity, and that this method can be used in clinical settings to assess the risk for cardiovascular disease.
the presented method can be applied to all screening CTs and it is able to provide a reliable assessment of cardiovascular risk in heavy smokers.
